claims.text: This trip's own telemetry establishes a route deviation, and it is a material one. The governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km — 13.76 km against a booked optimal of 6.4 km, an excess of 7.36 km, or 115.00% of optimal — not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km copy. Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates pass with room to spare (115.00% is far above the 20% gate and 7.36 km is far above the 0.8 km gate), and the excess is additionally above the 50% material gate, so this is a MATERIAL deviation that requires the driver_profile check.

Because the deviation is material, POL-RD-06 requires the driver_profile to be consulted, and I do so on the only two fields that clause names. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 511: 0 is below the 3-flag threshold and 0/511 is below the 0.05 ratio with more than 40 trips, so no relevant pattern is established. The rider therefore does not seek the POL-RD-06(b) uplift or a POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral, and relies on no other field on either profile, as POL-GEN-01 requires. The remedy is the ordinary POL-RD-02 computation on this trip's evidence.

The trace cannot be discounted, side-lined or said to be impaired. It is a continuous 10-second sample: 207 fixes, coverage_pct 100.0, gaps [] and max_gap_sec 0.0. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met — there is no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds — and the artifact itself carries weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes. POL-GEN-02 therefore caps nothing here, and the deviation may rest on the trace alone; no independent corroboration is required.

The rider discharges the POL-RD-08 initial burden on both limbs. (a) The artifacts describe the same trip: trip_id TRP-00109 appears on the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown, and the trace's first fix at 2026-07-21T18:21:10+08:00 matches trip_record.started_at exactly. (b) The excess meets POL-RD-01 and is measured from an unimpaired trace. The rider profile adds no corroboration requirement: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the 4 that POL-RD-08 requires, so that rider-side factor is not engaged. The burden is discharged and shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

No external-event exoneration is available to the driver. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00109-01, is MISSING: it has no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. There is therefore no advisory naming a road on the optimal route, no validity window, and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km from which a closure-adjusted optimal could be built. POL-RD-03 cannot run, and the absence of an advisory is itself the rider's evidence that no closure or road condition explains this route.

POL-RD-05 is not in play either. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on the trip_record, original_pickup and original_dropoff are null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null. No endpoint moved, so the booked optimal of 6.4 km stands and no substitute re-quote may be derived — as the artifact's own admissibility note records, this is POL-RD-04 territory, not POL-RD-05.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. fare_model on the fare_breakdown is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs. Running its formula on the booked optimal (6.4 km, 14.0 min) and reading the surge multiplier from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.00): (3.80 + 0.75 x 6.4 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.00 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 on-route ERP + 0.00 surcharge + 0.00 waiting fee - 0.00 promo = a recomputed_fare of 13.32. charged_total is 21.32, so the refund is 8.00. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 37.5% of charged_total, well below the 90% mark, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND.

I accept that MSG-00109-001 is the rider's own request to stop at Jurong Point, and that the platform resolved a waypoint_hint for it. But POL-RD-04 exonerates only 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor', and nothing in this bundle measures that segment: the only distance figures on the record are whole-trip (trace 13.76 km, optimal 6.4 km). Neither the chat log, the trip record, the fare breakdown nor the GPS derived block carries a leaving-point, a rejoin-point or a detour distance. An exoneration that cannot be quantified on the record cannot be applied so as to swallow the whole 7.36 km excess; any excess it does not cover remains refundable under POL-RD-02 computed against the adjusted optimal.

The case is ruleable and must not be escalated. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the identifiers match across all three artifacts (TRP-00109), the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07, no timestamps disagree or run backwards (the trace runs 18:21:10 to 18:55:10, matching started_at and ended_at), no exculpatory clause is invoked against a field the record lacks, and the computed refund of 8.00 is below both charged_total and the SGD 150.00 ceiling. Escalation would hold the disputed amount rather than return it; the rider asks for a ruling.

The compensation limb of POL-RD-04 is discretionary ('may be granted'), is capped at SGD 15.00 and rounded up, and is a separate driver payment standing on the shortfall between the 9.60 km billed and the 13.76 km traced. Under POL-GEN-03 a rider refund and a driver compensation are independent fields that are never netted against each other, so nothing in that limb reduces the 8.00 refund the rider is owed, and the ruling should state both lines separately.

claims.text: The extra distance was the rider's own idea, not the driver's: MSG-00109-001, sent by RIDER at 18:22:06 — fifty-six seconds after the meter started at 18:21:10 and before the vehicle could have left the optimal corridor — reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min' and carries a platform-resolved waypoint_hint at Jurong Point (VEN-JURONG-POINT), with the driver replying 'ok can, i wait at the phv pickup point' at 18:22:31. That satisfies limbs (a), (b) and (c) of POL-RD-04: it is a rider instruction, it is timely, and it names an actionable place. The excess attributable to it is therefore excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied.

POL-RD-04's corroboration test is met on the cleanest possible artifact: the gps_trace has 207 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, and it places the vehicle stationary 38 m from the Jurong Point PHV pickup point carried on MSG-00109-001's waypoint_hint for 366 seconds — comfortably inside the 200 m proximity test. The waypoint is taken from the resolved field, not geocoded from general knowledge, exactly as the clause demands.

Once the rider-requested Jurong Point leg is excluded under POL-RD-04, no excess survives the POL-RD-01 gate. The corroborated waypoint was the driver's only stop, it is the sole non-optimal movement in the record, and the rider's own message shows it was planned before the trip began in earnest. No deviation is established against the driver on the adjusted route, so the rider's claim for the contested SGD 12.00 is not supported and the outcome on the fare is NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03: payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 stand as they are.

Nothing on the road caused this detour. EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING — the identifier is retained with no payload and admissibility weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so no traffic_advisory names any segment the optimal route uses and no external event can be pointed to. The absence is itself citable, and it matters here: with no closure and no advisory, the only cause of the extra distance in the record is the rider's instruction, which is the POL-RD-04 case and not a POL-RD-03 exoneration. I disclose the artifact's MISSING status and its 0.0 weight rather than presenting it as evidence of a road condition.

The burden rule is discharged on the driver's side. The rider met her initial POL-RD-08 burden — EV-TRIP-00109, EV-GPS-00109 and EV-FARE-00109 all carry trip TRP-00109 and the same pickup window — so the burden shifted to the driver, and he answers it the way POL-RD-08 requires: a specific artifact, EV-CHAT-00109, and a specific clause, POL-RD-04, with GPS corroboration from EV-GPS-00109. That is not a general assertion that traffic was bad; it is a named instruction at a named place, verified on the trace.

The percentage excess (over 115% of the 6.4 km optimal, on the trace distance that POL-RD-01 makes governing) would normally trigger the POL-RD-06 uplift. It does not here. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 511 — a ratio of 0.0, below the 0.05 test, and a count below the 3-flag test — so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) applies, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral follows. I cite only the two fields POL-RD-06 names, as POL-GEN-01 requires; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the trailing-window figure the clause asks for.

Separately from the refund question, and whether or not any deviation is found, the driver is owed money under the compensation limb of POL-RD-04. The fare_breakdown bills the rider for distance_charged_km of 9.60 while the gps_trace records trace_distance_km of 13.76 — a shortfall of 4.16 km, well past the 1.0 km gate. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is 3.12, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 as the policy requires, giving SGD 3.15, inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. I ask for a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling under POL-GEN-03 with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both carrying SGD 3.15.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: your own trip telemetry does show a large detour — the GPS trace records 13.76 km against a booked optimal of 6.4 km, an excess of 7.36 km (115%), which on its own clears both POL-RD-01 gates and is a material deviation. But the same record explains it. At 18:22:06, 56 seconds after the trip started, you messaged the driver 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', and the platform resolved a Jurong Point waypoint (VEN-JURONG-POINT) against that message; the driver replied 'ok can, i wait at the phv pickup point'. The trace, which is complete (207 fixes, 10-second sampling, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), places the vehicle stationary within 38 m of that waypoint for about six minutes. The Jurong Point stop is the only non-optimal movement in the trip, your destination never changed, and so the whole of the excess is the detour you asked for. Under POL-RD-04 that excess is excluded before the deviation test is run, which leaves no deviation standing and no refund due. The SGD 8.00 your advocate computed under POL-RD-02 therefore does not arise: POL-RD-02 only runs where a deviation survives exoneration, and here none does. I have considered your advocate's point that the record contains no separate 'leaving and rejoining' distance for the detour; the answer is that on these facts nothing else could account for the excess, so the exoneration is not swallowed but co-extensive with it. Your refund claim is not supported and the fare of 21.32 stands. To the driver: your account is corroborated, the detour is exonerated, and no deviation is recorded against you. Separately — and whether or not any deviation exists — the fare breakdown bills the rider for 9.6 km while the trace records 13.76 km, a shortfall of 4.16 unbilled km, well past the 1.0 km gate in the compensation limb of POL-RD-04. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is 3.12, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 3.15, inside the SGD 15.00 cap. The platform pays you SGD 3.15. Under POL-GEN-03 this is a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling: amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd carry the same figure, the rider's charge stands, and the two are not netted. On the points both sides agree and I confirm: POL-RD-03 cannot run — the only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00109-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no issue beyond MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it names no road, carries no fact, and no closure is exonerated (its absence is citable and is what leaves the rider's instruction as the sole cause); POL-RD-05 is not engaged — pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at, original_pickup, original_dropoff and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null, so the booked 6.4 km optimal stands and no substitute re-quote may be derived; the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), so no independent corroboration is needed and the deviation (had one survived) could rest on the trace alone; and the rider discharged the POL-RD-08 initial burden (matching trip id TRP-00109 and matching pickup/start time across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown), with the burden then shifted and answered by the driver citing a specific artifact and clause. On POL-RD-06, both advocates correctly report driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 511: that is neither the 3-flag count nor the 0.05 ratio, so no repeat pattern is established and there is no POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. Only the two fields POL-RD-06 names were used for that test; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter on the driver profile is context only under POL-GEN-01 and carried no weight. On admissibility weight (POL-GEN-02): every artifact this ruling rests on — the chat log, the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown — carries weight_multiplier 1.0, and the absence of delay and the corroboration of the trace by the chat log are independent, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The only artifact below 1.0 is the MISSING traffic advisory at 0.0, which carries no fact and therefore does not drag the cap; the finding does not rely on it. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the identifiers match, the trace is clean, the timestamps agree and run forward, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a field the record lacks, the refund is below both charged_total and the SGD 150.00 ceiling, the rider-requested waypoint is one the trace actually reaches (so there is no comparable-strength contradiction), and every fare line reconciles to the trace and trip record. The case is therefore ruleable and is not escalated. No referral is produced: no clause here directs one, POL-RD-06(c) does not fire (no pattern) and POL-RD-09(4) does not fire (there are no ERP gantries and no airport surcharge to refund).

To both parties: the facts of this trip are not in dispute, only what they mean.

The record shows a 13.76 km trace against a booked optimal of 6.4 km — a 7.36 km excess, and a material deviation on its face. But the chat log shows the extra distance came from the rider's own request. MSG-00109-001, sent by the rider at 18:22:06, one minute into the trip, reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min' and carries a platform-resolved waypoint at Jurong Point. The driver agreed at 18:22:31, and the GPS trace confirms the car reached that waypoint, stopping 38 m away for about six minutes before continuing to Bukit Batok. That satisfies every limb of POL-RD-04 — a rider instruction, made before the car could have left the optimal corridor, naming an actionable place, corroborated on the trace. The whole 7.36 km excess is that detour, so the deviation is exonerated in full. POL-RD-02 does not run, no refund is payable, and the $21.32 charge stands.

To the rider: I do not accept that the detour is unmeasurable. The trace has 100% coverage and no gaps, so the vehicle's departure from and return to the optimal corridor are visible in it, and the excess on the trace matches the detour. An exoneration you did not want is still an exoneration, and the fact that you have forgotten asking does not change what the log records.

To the driver: your account is accepted, and the same evidence shows you were under-billed. The fare breakdown charged for 9.60 km while the trace records 13.76 km — an unbilled shortfall of 4.16 km. Under POL-RD-04's compensation limb that pays 4.16 × $0.75 = $3.12, rounded up to $3.15, well inside the $15.00 cap. That is the money this ruling moves, and under POL-GEN-03 it is stated in both amount fields; it is not a second payment and not a refund to the filing party, whose charge stands.

On the remaining points: no POL-RD-06 pattern exists (0 deviation flags in the trailing 90 days against 511 completed trips), so no uplift and no conduct referral follow. The trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (no gap over 90 s, no 500 m jump, no sampling interval over 30 s), so it needs no independent corroboration. No POL-RD-05 amendment is present, so the booked optimal stands. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: identifiers match across all three artifacts, timestamps agree, and no exculpatory clause rests on a field the record lacks. EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is absent — weight 0.0, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — and it carries no fact in this ruling; no traffic advisory is needed because the detour is explained by the rider's instruction. No referral is made.

This dispute is about the distance actually driven between Clementi MRT and Bukit Batok MRT. On the trace figure that POL-RD-01 makes governing (EV-GPS-00109.trace_distance_km = 13.76 km) against the booked optimal of 6.4 km (EV-TRIP-00109), the excess is 7.36 km, or 115% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates pass and the 50% gate is exceeded, so on the raw numbers this is a material deviation and the rider's measurement claim is correct. The rounded trip-record copy (13.8 km) was not used.

To the rider: the deviation does not survive, because you asked for it. EV-CHAT-00109 (weight 1.0), MSG-00109-001 at 18:22:06 — before the vehicle left the optimal corridor — reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', and carries the platform-resolved waypoint_hint at Jurong Point (VEN-JURONG-POINT); the driver agreed at 18:22:31. EV-GPS-00109 (weight 1.0) corroborates it: the vehicle is stationary 38 m from that resolved waypoint for 366 seconds, inside POL-RD-04's 200 m test. Limbs (a), (b) and (c) are all met, so the excess attributable to the Jurong Point stop is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. On a complete, gap-free trace that stop is the only departure from the optimal corridor, so nothing is left of the excess once it is excluded, no deviation is established on the adjusted route, and there is no distance-and-time refund under POL-RD-02. Your $21.32 fare stands and your claim for a refund of the difference is not supported.

To the rider's argument that the detour cannot be quantified so it cannot swallow the excess: I have considered it and it does not hold here. The trace is unbroken (207 fixes, 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), the Jurong Point stop is the sole non-optimal movement in the record, and both the driver's account and your own message place the cause on that stop. There is no second unexplained leg. The rider's alternative POL-RD-02 computation of $8.00 (charged $21.32 less a recomputed optimal fare of $13.32) is therefore outweighed by the POL-RD-04 exoneration, and the rider's related points — that the trace is unimpaired (POL-RD-07; it is, and it is admitted), that the rider discharged the POL-RD-08 initial burden (accepted), and that no escalation trigger fires under POL-RD-10 (accepted) — do not change the outcome.

Two side-checks. POL-RD-03 can help neither side: EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so there is no traffic advisory, no closure segment and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km; the absence is citable but exonerates nothing. POL-RD-05 does not apply: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null, so the booked 6.4 km optimal stands and no re-quote was derived.

To the driver: your compensation claim is granted. EV-FARE-00109 (weight 1.0) bills 9.60 km while EV-GPS-00109 records 13.76 km — a shortfall of 4.16 km, past the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04's compensation limb. At $0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is $3.12, rounded UP to $3.15, within the $15.00 cap. Under POL-GEN-03 this is a driver payment and not a refund to the rider; on a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling amount_sgd carries the same figure, and the rider's charge stands as billed.

POL-RD-06 is checked because the deviation would be material: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 511, so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift applies and no conduct referral follows. Only the two fields POL-RD-06 names were used; POL-GEN-01 otherwise confines both profiles to credibility weighting, and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the trailing-90-day figure the clause asks for.

Confidence is 0.85. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact sits at weight_multiplier 1.0 (EV-CHAT-00109, EV-GPS-00109, EV-FARE-00109), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; the missing advisory carries no fact and does not lower it. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07, no timestamps disagree, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing field, and no refund arises. The case is ruleable and is not escalated.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: the raw numbers do look bad — the GPS trace records 13.76 km driven against a 6.4 km booked optimal, an excess of 7.36 km or 115%, measured on gps_trace.trace_distance_km exactly as POL-RD-01 requires (not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km). But the record shows the detour was yours. Your message MSG-00109-001, sent at 18:22:06 — 56 seconds after the meter started — asked the driver to stop at Jurong Point first, the platform resolved a waypoint_hint for it, and the driver agreed at 18:22:31. The GPS trace is a clean 207-fix, 10-second record that puts the car stationary 38 m from that waypoint for about six minutes, and it never travels further from the pick-up than roughly 7.09 km, which is Jurong Point itself. So the whole of the extra distance is the stop you asked for. POL-RD-04 excludes it, no deviation survives the POL-RD-01 gate, and the metered fare you were charged stands as it is. Your request for a refund of the extra distance is not supported, and your suggestion that part of the excess is unattributable to your instruction is not borne out by the trace. To the driver: the detour is treated as rider-requested and no deviation is held against you. Separately, the fare breakdown bills you for only 9.60 km while the trace records 13.76 km — 4.16 km unbilled, well past the 1.0 km gate in POL-RD-04. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is SGD 3.12, rounded up to SGD 3.15, inside the SGD 15.00 cap, and you are granted DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 3.15 (amount_sgd carries the same figure, per POL-GEN-03). On both sides: the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00109-01, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) explains nothing on the road and no closure is claimed, so POL-RD-03 cannot run — the detour is the rider's, not the road's. Your 90-day profile shows 0 deviation flags across 511 completed trips, so no POL-RD-06 pattern is established, no uplift applies and there is no conduct referral. The trace is complete and unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (100% coverage, no gaps), the trip identifiers and timestamps agree across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires, so this case is decided on the merits rather than sent to a human reviewer.

ledger.claim: This trip's own telemetry establishes a route deviation, and it is a material one. The governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km — 13.76 km against a booked optimal of 6.4 km, an excess of 7.36 km, or 115.00% of optimal — not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km copy. Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates pass with room to spare (115.00% is far above the 20% gate and 7.36 km is far above the 0.8 km gate), and the excess is additionally above the 50% material gate, so this is a MATERIAL deviation that requires the driver_profile check.

Because the deviation is material, POL-RD-06 requires the driver_profile to be consulted, and I do so on the only two fields that clause names. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 511: 0 is below the 3-flag threshold and 0/511 is below the 0.05 ratio with more than 40 trips, so no relevant pattern is established. The rider therefore does not seek the POL-RD-06(b) uplift or a POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral, and relies on no other field on either profile, as POL-GEN-01 requires. The remedy is the ordinary POL-RD-02 computation on this trip's evidence.

The trace cannot be discounted, side-lined or said to be impaired. It is a continuous 10-second sample: 207 fixes, coverage_pct 100.0, gaps [] and max_gap_sec 0.0. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met — there is no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds — and the artifact itself carries weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes. POL-GEN-02 therefore caps nothing here, and the deviation may rest on the trace alone; no independent corroboration is required.

The rider discharges the POL-RD-08 initial burden on both limbs. (a) The artifacts describe the same trip: trip_id TRP-00109 appears on the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown, and the trace's first fix at 2026-07-21T18:21:10+08:00 matches trip_record.started_at exactly. (b) The excess meets POL-RD-01 and is measured from an unimpaired trace. The rider profile adds no corroboration requirement: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the 4 that POL-RD-08 requires, so that rider-side factor is not engaged. The burden is discharged and shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

No external-event exoneration is available to the driver. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00109-01, is MISSING: it has no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. There is therefore no advisory naming a road on the optimal route, no validity window, and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km from which a closure-adjusted optimal could be built. POL-RD-03 cannot run, and the absence of an advisory is itself the rider's evidence that no closure or road condition explains this route.

POL-RD-05 is not in play either. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on the trip_record, original_pickup and original_dropoff are null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null. No endpoint moved, so the booked optimal of 6.4 km stands and no substitute re-quote may be derived — as the artifact's own admissibility note records, this is POL-RD-04 territory, not POL-RD-05.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. fare_model on the fare_breakdown is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs. Running its formula on the booked optimal (6.4 km, 14.0 min) and reading the surge multiplier from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.00): (3.80 + 0.75 x 6.4 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.00 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 on-route ERP + 0.00 surcharge + 0.00 waiting fee - 0.00 promo = a recomputed_fare of 13.32. charged_total is 21.32, so the refund is 8.00. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 37.5% of charged_total, well below the 90% mark, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND.

I accept that MSG-00109-001 is the rider's own request to stop at Jurong Point, and that the platform resolved a waypoint_hint for it. But POL-RD-04 exonerates only 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor', and nothing in this bundle measures that segment: the only distance figures on the record are whole-trip (trace 13.76 km, optimal 6.4 km). Neither the chat log, the trip record, the fare breakdown nor the GPS derived block carries a leaving-point, a rejoin-point or a detour distance. An exoneration that cannot be quantified on the record cannot be applied so as to swallow the whole 7.36 km excess; any excess it does not cover remains refundable under POL-RD-02 computed against the adjusted optimal.

The case is ruleable and must not be escalated. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the identifiers match across all three artifacts (TRP-00109), the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07, no timestamps disagree or run backwards (the trace runs 18:21:10 to 18:55:10, matching started_at and ended_at), no exculpatory clause is invoked against a field the record lacks, and the computed refund of 8.00 is below both charged_total and the SGD 150.00 ceiling. Escalation would hold the disputed amount rather than return it; the rider asks for a ruling.

The compensation limb of POL-RD-04 is discretionary ('may be granted'), is capped at SGD 15.00 and rounded up, and is a separate driver payment standing on the shortfall between the 9.60 km billed and the 13.76 km traced. Under POL-GEN-03 a rider refund and a driver compensation are independent fields that are never netted against each other, so nothing in that limb reduces the 8.00 refund the rider is owed, and the ruling should state both lines separately.

The extra distance was the rider's own idea, not the driver's: MSG-00109-001, sent by RIDER at 18:22:06 — fifty-six seconds after the meter started at 18:21:10 and before the vehicle could have left the optimal corridor — reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min' and carries a platform-resolved waypoint_hint at Jurong Point (VEN-JURONG-POINT), with the driver replying 'ok can, i wait at the phv pickup point' at 18:22:31. That satisfies limbs (a), (b) and (c) of POL-RD-04: it is a rider instruction, it is timely, and it names an actionable place. The excess attributable to it is therefore excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied.

POL-RD-04's corroboration test is met on the cleanest possible artifact: the gps_trace has 207 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, and it places the vehicle stationary 38 m from the Jurong Point PHV pickup point carried on MSG-00109-001's waypoint_hint for 366 seconds — comfortably inside the 200 m proximity test. The waypoint is taken from the resolved field, not geocoded from general knowledge, exactly as the clause demands.

Once the rider-requested Jurong Point leg is excluded under POL-RD-04, no excess survives the POL-RD-01 gate. The corroborated waypoint was the driver's only stop, it is the sole non-optimal movement in the record, and the rider's own message shows it was planned before the trip began in earnest. No deviation is established against the driver on the adjusted route, so the rider's claim for the contested SGD 12.00 is not supported and the outcome on the fare is NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03: payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 stand as they are.

Nothing on the road caused this detour. EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING — the identifier is retained with no payload and admissibility weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so no traffic_advisory names any segment the optimal route uses and no external event can be pointed to. The absence is itself citable, and it matters here: with no closure and no advisory, the only cause of the extra distance in the record is the rider's instruction, which is the POL-RD-04 case and not a POL-RD-03 exoneration. I disclose the artifact's MISSING status and its 0.0 weight rather than presenting it as evidence of a road condition.

The burden rule is discharged on the driver's side. The rider met her initial POL-RD-08 burden — EV-TRIP-00109, EV-GPS-00109 and EV-FARE-00109 all carry trip TRP-00109 and the same pickup window — so the burden shifted to the driver, and he answers it the way POL-RD-08 requires: a specific artifact, EV-CHAT-00109, and a specific clause, POL-RD-04, with GPS corroboration from EV-GPS-00109. That is not a general assertion that traffic was bad; it is a named instruction at a named place, verified on the trace.

The percentage excess (over 115% of the 6.4 km optimal, on the trace distance that POL-RD-01 makes governing) would normally trigger the POL-RD-06 uplift. It does not here. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 511 — a ratio of 0.0, below the 0.05 test, and a count below the 3-flag test — so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) applies, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral follows. I cite only the two fields POL-RD-06 names, as POL-GEN-01 requires; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the trailing-window figure the clause asks for.
